description: I am leading a team developing IGNIS AI, an AI-powered research platform focused on safer human space exploration. It uses NASA's microgravity combustion research to help users discover, understand, compare, and interpret scientific findings. Our goal is to make complex research accessible and generate evidence-based insights into flame behaviour and potential spacecraft fire-safety challenges.
summary:
IGNIS AI is a web-based research dashboard designed to make NASA's microgravity combustion research easier to explore, compare and understand. It brings relevant research records into one place, helping users examine experimental conditions, findings and the limitations of individual studies. The project focuses on how factors such as gravity, oxygen concentration, pressure, airflow and fuel properties influence flame behavior in space. Through an organized research library, study comparisons and an AI-assisted research interface, IGNIS AI aims to make scientific findings more accessible and help users explore their relevance to fire safety during future human missions to the Moon and Mars.
 The platform is intended as a research and learning tool, not a certified spacecraft fire-safety system.
details:
IGNIS AI addresses the difficulty of finding and understanding the large body of research on combustion in microgravity. NASA has conducted experiments involving flames, solid fuels, smoke, ignition and flame extinction in reduced-gravity environments. However, their findings are spread across different investigations and publications.

Our project organizes relevant research into a structured digital library. Each research record presents the investigation, its objectives, experimental conditions, findings, source references and limitations. Users can explore individual studies and compare their results while keeping differences in experimental conditions in mind.
Missing information is identified rather than assumed.

A central part of IGNIS AI is making scientific information more accessible. Its AI-assisted research interface is designed to answer questions using the project's research records, provide supporting references and distinguish reported observations from predictions or interpretations. It also aims to acknowledge uncertainty and avoid presenting limited experimental results as universal fire-safety rules.

The project is being developed as a web application using JavaScript, HTML, CSS and a Node.js backend, with GitHub for source-code management and Vercel for deployment. AI tools were used selectively for supporting tasks, including research organization, writing assistance, and some coding and debugging. The project’s concept, direction, research selection, and scientific review were led by the team.

The intended impact is to make microgravity combustion research easier to navigate and help students, researchers and space-safety audiences understand evidence relevant to future human space exploration. IGNIS AI is a research exploration tool and does not replace engineering validation or official spacecraft safety procedures.
